Sam: Quick sync — running an apples-to-apples bench between the replay harness and our synthetic generator across GPUs. A100 (driver 525) vs L40s (driver 535). Same container image, same model version, but replay shows ~18% higher p99 on the A100 run. Anyone seen this pattern?

Liam: How are you running the synthetic traffic? seq lengths / prefix / warm cache? Also which CUDA/cudnn in the image?

Sam: Synthetic is our new event-stream generator (batching=4, dynamic prefilling disabled). Replay is the trace-driven harness that replays real requests (KV warmed by default). Image + runtime info:
```
image: redwood/serving:2026-02-22-cuda11.8
nvidia-smi: driver 525.85.12
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
CUDA_VERSION=11.8
cmd: ./bin/bench --mode replay --trace s3://bench/traces/2026-02-21/trace-8241.json --batch-size 4 --concurrency 32
```
I also tried the same image on L40s with driver 535.30 and saw the gap persisted.

Jess: Important: replay preserves KV cache warm-up and prefix locality. Synthetic usually sends fresh contexts unless you explicitly prefill. That alone can change kernel selection (longer KV cache hits -> different attention kernel path). Did you try synthetic with a KV-prefill stage?

Tanwi: Also check our kernel selector heuristics — we have an env flag to force conservative kernel choices for deterministic comparison:
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_STRATEGY=conservative  # forces fallback-friendly kernels
REDWOOD_BATCHER_MODE=static  # disables dynamic batching heuristics
```
If replay is hitting a different kernel path due to sequence distribution, that would explain a p99 delta.

Sam: I tested batch sizes 1/4/8 and toggled REDWOOD_BATCHER_MODE. With static batching the gap shrank but didn't vanish (went from 18% -> ~8%).

perf-bot: 
Automated perf alert: p99 increased 18% on a100-prod-fleet between runs 2026-02-21 and 2026-02-22. Trace: https://perf.redwood.internal/alerts/alert-6721 (investigate KV warmup / kernel selection).

ops-qa: Also confirm container image includes the same CUDA/cuBLAS runtime bits. Minor driver/CUDA microversions can flip kernel heuristics. Recommend one narrow repro: same image, pinned driver version, fixed seq len (e.g., 512), and explicit KV prefill vs cold.

Liam: Another knob: TF32 and cuBLAS algo autotune. Try running with TF32=0 and KERNEL_AUTO_TUNE=0 to eliminate autotuning variance.

Tanwi: Quick repro command I used to verify kernel path differences on L40s: 
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_STRATEGY=traceable KERNEL_AUTO_TUNE=0 ./bin/bench --mode replay --trace trace.json --batch-size 4 --concurrency 16 --seq-len 512 --kv-prefill s3://bench/kv-warm/
# generates kernel-selection.log alongside perf profiles
```
Kernel-selection log shows which attention kernel variant was picked per step.

Sam: Good call. I'll run three configs across A100 and L40s tonight:
- replay (warm KV)
- synthetic (no prefill)
- replay (cold, no prefill)
Collect nvprof/cupti traces + kernel-selection.log + flamegraphs and upload to s3://bench/apples-1972345678. I'll also try TF32 off.

Jess: On it — scheduling the runs after 22:00 PST to avoid interfering with the nightly load tests.

Sam: Action items summarized:
1) Run narrow repro on both GPU types with pinned driver/CUDA and same image.
2) Produce kernel-selection logs and nvprof traces.
3) Try TF32=0 and KERNEL_AUTO_TUNE=0.
4) Compare replay-warm vs synthetic to isolate KV cache effect.
Upload artifacts to s3 and ping this thread. cc @Jess to own runs. :thumbsup:

Liam: If you want, I can add a small harness to force identical prefix distributions between synthetic/replay to make the comparison more apples-to-apples.

Sam: Please do. I'll post the first artifact links here when done. Thanks! :raised_hands:
